<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ui/reports.mdx`  _(via queryDataset (sdk, the bare tail of client method analytics.queryDataset, bound to POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via queryDataset (sdk, the bare tail of client method analytics.queryDataset, bound to POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via analytics.queryDataset (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query), queryDataset (sdk, the bare tail of client method analytics.queryDataset, bound to POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via queryDataset (sdk, the bare tail of client method analytics.queryDataset, bound to POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v9.mdx`  _(via queryDataset (sdk, the bare tail of client method analytics.queryDataset, bound to POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 45 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **246** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **181** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **181**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **122** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d391babc3c2e741b222439180e4b9e49e6b533ee` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e046c6ab8bc7e2cf5c30a6fb1913e66d29b9b2c8` — the merge of head `c043839cf9b3014db959cd51a9f1d9c12888fecc` into base `d391babc3c2e741b222439180e4b9e49e6b533ee`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e046c6ab8bc7e2cf5c30a6fb1913e66d29b9b2c8 && git checkout e046c6ab8bc7e2cf5c30a6fb1913e66d29b9b2c8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d391babc3c2e741b222439180e4b9e49e6b533ee c043839cf9b3014db959cd51a9f1d9c12888fecc && git checkout -B drift-repro d391babc3c2e741b222439180e4b9e49e6b533ee && git merge --no-ff c043839cf9b3014db959cd51a9f1d9c12888fecc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d391babc3c2e741b222439180e4b9e49e6b533ee
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d391babc3c2e741b222439180e4b9e49e6b533ee` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6f52e2fd9d300ca2907f69f44a52ee1a63a3f901`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/analytics.zod.ts + packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json

Read for this record: card #32203 (body and its 4 comments: the claim, amendments 1 and 2, the dev report 6770143037), PR #32251 (body, 12-file list), the net diff `origin/main...6f52e2fd`, and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `packages/rest/src/analytics-routes.ts`, `analytics-dataset-body-door.ts`, `analytics-selection-door.ts`, `error-response.ts`, `packages/spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts`, `record-page.zod.ts`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`. The rest of the diff (the test file, generated baselines and reference pages, the strictness count, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface: 10 new exports, nothing removed or changed. Right.** `api-surface/api.json` gains `DATASET_QUERY_BATCH_MAX_QUERIES`, three `DatasetQueryBatch*Schema` consts and their six types. No existing line of `analytics.zod.ts` moves except the import of `ApiErrorSchema`.
- **Accept-set of the single door: unchanged. Right.** `DatasetSelectionSchema` and `AnalyticsResultResponseSchema` are untouched in the diff; the batch takes `AnalyticsResultResponseSchema.shape.data` by reference and re-describes a clone.
- **New accept-sets.** Request: a strict object with `queries`, an array of 1 to 50 JSON objects. Entry: a union of two strict arms, `data` or `status` (integer 400 to 599) plus `error`. Response: `BaseResponseSchema` plus a required strict `data.results`. All three are additions.
- **Metadata-protocol: `added` is the right reading (seat point 1).** `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` gains 5 keys (`DatasetQueryBatchRequest:queries`, `DatasetQueryBatchResponse:data|error|meta|success`). That ledger records the keys of every published object schema in `api/`, wire bodies included, and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses `none` whenever a shard under `packages/spec/authorable-surface/` moves (verdict `none-baseline-moved`). The card's `none` was an estimate from the meaning of the word "authorable"; the gate measures the ledger, and the ledger moved. Claim amendment 2 already carries `added`. `DatasetQueryBatchEntry` adds no key because a union has no top-level members.
- **Dropped-refinements header 263 / 1050: right (seat point 3, second half).** `main` reads 261 / 1048. The head's `entries` hold 263 schemas and 1050 sites (counted from the committed file), so the hand-set header equals the body. The two new rows are the one existing site of `api/AnalyticsResultResponse` (`data.drillScopes.valueType.lazy`, the lazy `FilterConditionSchema`), reached through the reused `data` member, and their paths follow the ledger's own spelling (`options[0]`, `element`). No new refinement is written by this diff. `DatasetQueryBatchRequest` rightly has no row.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening)

`@objectstack/spec` minor matches what the diff publishes: new exports and three new published JSON Schemas, no existing accept-set narrowed. The changeset and the PR body both carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`; the `Check Changeset` run on this head completed `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report. Nothing to answer.
- Premise correction 1 (the single door answers the bare `AnalyticsResult`, not the envelope): **confirmed.** `analytics-routes.ts` ends `res.json(result)`. Carrying `shape.data` in an answered entry is right.
- Premise correction 2 (the single door's outer body has no spec schema): **confirmed.** It is judged by `DATASET_QUERY_BODY_KEYS` in `analytics-dataset-body-door.ts`; `DatasetSelectionSchema` covers `selection` alone.
- Out-of-scope note, `detail` (singular) on the "Invalid dataset definition." 400: confirmed, and it is the smallest of a wider gap. See ④ finding 1, which this record raises to should-fix.
- Out-of-scope note, the batch sentence owed in `content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx`: accepted as carried by #32200.
- Hand-set `measured` header after the merge: judged right in ①.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/analytics.zod.ts`**, against the card's four asks and the single door it cites.

What holds:

- **Request (seat point 2).** The card asks for "an ordered list of the existing single selections". A selection alone does not name its dataset, so an entry has to be the whole single-door body, and that body has no spec schema. Declaring each entry as an opaque JSON object is the design that keeps "one refused item never fails the others" true: a typed entry would make one malformed selection a whole-batch parse failure. Tries to break it: an entry of `{}` is accepted here and refused per entry by the door (`body.selection.measures must be a non-empty array`); a `null`, string or array entry is refused whole, as documented; an empty list and 51 entries are refused whole; a key beside `queries` is refused (`strict`), which stops a batch-level `previewDrafts` from being silently dropped; two identical entries are both answered.
- **Bound.** `RECORD_PAGE_MAX_RELATED` is 50 in `record-page.zod.ts`, as the jsdoc says. The card left the number to the lane.
- **Naming by position (seat point 3, first half).** The card allows "an id or its index". Position needs no uniqueness rule, so there is rightly no duplicate-id refusal and no refinement of this PR's own.
- **Entry.** Both arms are strict, so `{ data, status, error }`, `{}` and `{ error }` alone are all refused. A refused query cannot parse as an empty answer.
- **Permissions.** The published describe text on a query says it is "judged exactly as that door judges it, as the same caller", which is what the card asked the describe text to state.

Findings:

1. **should-fix: the entry says `error` is the single door's refusal body with "the same code, message and details", and the cited door does not answer in that shape.** Three of the door's own answers do not parse as `ApiErrorSchema`, which requires `code` from the closed vocabulary and `message`:
   - its undeclared-fault answer is `res.status(500).json({ code: 'ANALYTICS_QUERY_FAILED', error: outward })`: the text is under `error`, and there is no `message`;
   - its declared-4xx arm answers `{ code: envelopeCode, message }` with the thrown code as written, so a code outside the closed vocabulary reaches the wire there, and `ApiErrorSchema` refuses it;
   - the `detail` key the dev noted is stripped by a parse.
   The schema is right to use the house envelope, which is what the card asks for. The sentences are wrong: the jsdoc ("refused here with the same code, status and message"), the entry jsdoc, and the published describe on `error`. A server that follows them and relays the door's body yields an entry its own contract refuses, in the fault case the per-entry design exists for. Fix in this file: say that the batch door maps each single-door refusal into `ApiErrorSchema` (the 500 text becomes `message`; a code outside the vocabulary moves to `declaredCode`, the rule `ApiErrorSchema` already states), and drop "the same".
2. **should-fix: `status` beside `error` is a second place for a fact `ApiErrorSchema` already carries.** `ApiErrorSchema.httpStatus` exists, and its jsdoc names this exact case: it is "load-bearing where this envelope rides response DATA rather than the response line", on a batch row. As written, `{ status: 403, error: { httpStatus: 404, ... } }` parses, and nothing says which one a client reads. Either state the rule in the jsdoc and describe text (`status` is the authority; `error.httpStatus`, if present, equals it), or carry the status on `error.httpStatus` alone as the record batch does. The first is the smaller change.
3. **nit: `data.results` has no length bound**, while the jsdoc says it has exactly as many entries as the request (1 to 50). An empty `results` parses. The sibling response schemas are equally loose; leave it or carry it.
4. **nit: `DatasetQueryBatchRequest['queries']` is typed as an array of string-keyed records of unknown**, so the exported type gives a client author no help with an entry. The `@objectstack/client` method in #32200 has to type its own parameter. Carry to #32200.
5. **nit: the contract is silent on `?preview=draft`.** The single door reads the draft flag from the query string as well as the body. Whether the batch URL honours it for every entry is #32200's decision; one sentence here would close it.
6. **nit: a whole-request refusal that depends on no query "answers with the status the single door answers it with"**, but the body shape is not stated. The single door's 501 and 404 bodies are bare `{ code, message }`, not the house envelope the malformed-batch refusal uses. Carry to #32200.

**`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`** agrees with the schema: two inherited rows, header equal to the body. No finding.

**Check-runs on `6f52e2fd`, as read when this record was written** (45 runs; in-progress runs are not counted as green):

- Completed `success` (14): Auto Label, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, Check Documentation Links, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, filter, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Flag docs affected by code changes, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards.
- Completed `skipped` (9): Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, Dogfood Regression Gate (shard matrix), UI Published Artifacts, Packed-tarball smoke, Borrowed queue verdict, Queue verdict, Schedule gate, 18.x upgrade harness.
- **Still in progress (22): Test Core 1/8 to 8/8 (8 runs), Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup and corpus.**
- None completed `failure`.

The gates that decide the generated baselines (the schema build that enforces the dropped-refinements ledger, the spec tests, the type checks) had not reported. This verdict is on the design and the committed tree; it does not stand in for those runs, and the seat reads them before the PR moves.

No must-fix. Findings 1 and 2 are should-fix and each earns a delta review of its fix; both fixes are in `analytics.zod.ts` text and regenerate the reference page and the published descriptions.

## Delta review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2d073d9ad340f4bc42e134046f8a8d4d6bc7bb27`
Base-record: comment 6770516195 on `6f52e2fd…`
Local-runs: none
Verdict: PASS

Read for this record: the one commit `6f52e2fd..2d073d9a` (3 files, +42 −9), and at this head `packages/spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts` (`ApiErrorSchema`), `errors.zod.ts` (`HttpStatusErrorCodeMap`, `standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus`), `error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, `packages/rest/src/analytics-routes.ts` (the dataset door's catch), `error-response.ts`, `analytics-dataset-body-door.ts`, `analytics-selection-door.ts`, `packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts` and `data-error-classification.ts`. Nothing was built or run.

### Should-fix 1 (the "same code, message and details" claim): closed

- "The same" is gone from all three places: the request jsdoc, the entry jsdoc and the published describe on `error`. No copy of the old sentences is left in the tree at this head, the changeset included.
- The new text says `error` is the refusal mapped into `ApiErrorSchema`, "not the door's response body relayed as it is". Each statement was checked against the tree:
  - `declaredCode` exists on `ApiErrorSchema` (optional string). Its jsdoc states the rule the new prose cites: a code outside the vocabulary is demoted there and `code` carries the member the HTTP status derives, through `resolveThrownHttpError` in `@objectstack/types`. The citation "the rule `ApiErrorSchema` states for every door" is accurate.
  - The undeclared-fault answer is `res.status(500).json({ code: 'ANALYTICS_QUERY_FAILED', error: outward, ...markExtra })`, so "`{ code, error }` with no `message`" is true, and `outward` is the already-withheld text, so "withheld as the door withholds it" is true.
  - `ANALYTICS_QUERY_FAILED` and `VALIDATION_FAILED` are registered in `error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, so the entries the new test expects to parse can parse.
  - `details.fields[]` is what the body door and the selection door answer on a validation refusal.
- A server door can do this mapping from what the single door produces: the status, the code and the text are all in hand at each arm, and the demotion rule is an exported function the door's own helpers already call.
- No new false claim found. Two gaps in the mapping remain; see findings 1 and 2.

### Should-fix 2 (`status` beside `error.httpStatus`): closed

- `httpStatus` exists on `ApiErrorSchema` (optional integer). Its jsdoc says the response status is authoritative and the field is "optional and redundant on purpose".
- The entry jsdoc and the published describe on `status` now say `status` is the authority and `error.httpStatus`, when present, equals it. `status` stays required. This is the first of the two options the base record offered, and it agrees with the envelope's own rule.
- Prose only, no refinement: acceptable, not a must-fix. A refinement on the arm cannot be stated in the published JSON Schema, so it would add a dropped-refinements row for a field that is optional and redundant by its own contract. A client that reads `status`, as the text tells it to, is never misled by a mismatch. `{ status: 403, error: { httpStatus: 404 } }` still parses; that is now a stated producer rule, not an open question.

### Other movement

- Accept-sets: unchanged. The only code lines that moved in `analytics.zod.ts` are the two `.describe()` strings; no `z.` shape, bound or `strict()` changed.
- Exports: unchanged. `api-surface`, `export-origins`, `declaration-map` and `authorable-surface` did not move and did not need to.
- `json-schema.manifest/api.json`: did not move and should not have. It lists schema names only, no describe text. The `packages/spec/json-schema/` tree that holds descriptions is gitignored.
- `dropped-refinements.baseline.json`: did not move, correctly, since no refinement was added.
- The one committed artifact that carries describe text is `content/docs/references/api/analytics.mdx`. Its two changed rows equal the two new describe strings character for character. No other file at this head holds the old or the new text.
- CI: `check:docs` (which re-renders that page) and `check:authorable-surface` both run in `Type Check · source gates`, which was still in progress. A stale reference page would be caught there, not by the `check:generated` step, which only reconciles the script ledger.
- Tests: one new case, 15 in the file.

### Findings

1. **should-fix (non-blocking; here or carried to #32200): the mapping names one `error`-keyed answer, and the door has more.** A declared server fault and a sandboxed fault answer through `declaredServerFaultAnswer` / `sandboxFaultAnswer`, whose body is `{ error, code?, declaredCode? }`: text under `error`, no `message`, and no `code` at all when the producer declared a status only (`thrownCodeFields` returns `{}`; `{ status: 503 }` is the documented case). The `message` bullet reads as if only the undeclared fault lacks `message`, and the `code` bullet covers a code that is not a member but not an absent one. The schema still forces both fields, so no wrong entry can parse; what is unstated is which member fills a missing `code`. One sentence closes it: every 5xx text the door carries under `error` becomes `message`, and an answer with no code takes the member the status derives.
2. **nit: `userMessage` is not in the list the batch door "writes".** The door answers it on three arms (`markExtra`), and `ApiErrorSchema` declares it as the end-user channel. The three bullets read as the whole mapping, so a door following them drops it. Same for singular `detail` on "Invalid dataset definition.", which the base record already noted.
3. **nit: the new test's demotion fixture contradicts the rule it illustrates.** It pins `status: 422` with `code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED'` beside a `declaredCode`. `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap` has no 422, so the status-derived member is `VALIDATION_ERROR`. The case parses either way; the fixture shows an entry the stated rule never yields. Use `VALIDATION_ERROR`, or `409` with `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`.
4. **nit: the PR body still says 14 tests**, in the summary and in the two-minute check. The file has 15.
5. **nit: no pin that a mismatched `error.httpStatus` still parses.** The rule is prose only by design; a one-line test would record that the schema does not enforce it.

No must-fix.

### Check-runs at this head

Read twice on `2d073d9a`; the second read is reported. 37 runs, none `failure`.

- Completed `success` (12): Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, filter, Dogfood Regression Gate.
- Completed `skipped` (9): Temporal Conformance, UI Published Artifacts, Dogfood Regression Gate (shard matrix), Dogfood Verify CLI, Borrowed queue verdict, Queue verdict, Schedule gate, 18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke.
- **Still in progress (16): Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Lint · ESLint, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure.**
- Not yet created: the Test Core shards (their plan job had not finished).

The runs that decide this delta had not reported: `Type Check · source gates` (reference page against describe text) and the spec tests (the new case). In-progress is not green; the seat reads them before the PR moves.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:spec#3 · head `c043839cf9`

- **Scope:** 12 files, +490 / −11, all inside the claim's surface.
